hints: One fine gives the right total and two give NaN: something goes wrong only when two amounts are added. The total is `finesDue(...)` in `client/src/format.ts`, called by `client/src/pages/ReaderPage.tsx`.

Marcus says the API sends `"fine": "1.00"`, a string. But `Loan` in `client/src/api/types.ts` says `fine: number`, so `total + loan.fine` looks like a sum to TypeScript. In JavaScript, `0 + "1.00"` is the string `"01.00"`, and `"01.00" + "0.75"` is `"01.000.75"`: not a number. With one fine, `"01.00"` still reads as 1.

Make the type say the truth, `fine: string` (dollars as decimal text), and turn each fine into a number before adding: `total + Number(loan.fine)`. TypeScript then shows you every other place that relies on `fine` being a number.
